mesh.title: Mesh Network Firmware
mesh.subtitle: Plug in a router — it builds the network itself
mesh.meta_desc: Free OpenWrt mesh firmware: seamless WiFi roaming, free guest network with VPN, auto-configuration. Download for GL.iNet, Asus, TP-Link routers.
mesh.hero_desc: Flash your router, power it on — it auto-configures mesh networking, private WiFi, guest network with bandwidth limits, and batman-adv routing. No manual setup needed.
mesh.benefit_seamless_desc: Walk between rooms — your device switches access points without dropping connection. 802.11r fast roaming across all nodes.
mesh.benefit_free_wifi_desc: Open network for neighbors and visitors. Speed-limited to 512 kbps, fully isolated from your private LAN.
mesh.benefit_privacy_desc: Guest traffic leaves through a VPN tunnel, never from your home IP address.
mesh.benefit_zero_config_desc: Unique network name, subnets, and encryption keys generated from MAC address at first boot. Just plug in.
mesh.benefit_remote_desc: Monitor, configure WiFi, run diagnostics — all from the Parahub IoT dashboard. No port forwarding needed.
mesh.benefit_earn_desc: Guests who want full speed pay satoshis via Lightning. The router lifts the throttle instantly. You earn without lifting a finger.
mesh.factory_desc: Use this if your router runs stock firmware
mesh.sysupgrade_desc: Use this if your router already runs OpenWrt
mesh.role_bumblebee_desc: Full gateway — internet access, VPN, guest network
mesh.role_bee_desc: Mesh relay — extends coverage, 10 Mbps for the host
mesh.pkg_mesh: Routers connect to each other automatically over WiFi
mesh.pkg_wifi: Dual-band mesh backhaul (2.4 GHz for range, 5 GHz for speed)
mesh.pkg_guest: Open guest network with 512 kbps limit and full isolation
mesh.pkg_private: Your private WPA3 network with seamless roaming
mesh.pkg_yggdrasil: Encrypted overlay for remote management without port forwarding
mesh.pkg_vpn: WireGuard VPN for guest traffic (Mullvad exit node)
mesh.pkg_speed_control: Per-client speed shaping with Lightning-paid upgrade to full speed
mesh.pkg_doh: Encrypted DNS for guests (DNS-over-HTTPS via Cloudflare)
mesh.pkg_luci: LuCI web interface for advanced settings
mesh.pkg_host_speed: 10 Mbps internet for the node host — incentive for extending mesh coverage
mesh.boot_step1: Unique hostname generated from MAC address (e.g. Parahub-A3F7)
mesh.boot_step2: Private and guest subnets derived from MAC (collision-free across nodes)
mesh.boot_step3: Shared mesh key pre-configured — nodes connect automatically
mesh.boot_step4: 5 wireless interfaces created: 2 mesh backhaul + 3 access points
mesh.boot_step5: Firewall isolates guest network from private LAN
mesh.boot_step6: Credentials saved to /etc/parahub/keys on the router
mesh.flash_glinet: Use U-Boot recovery. Connect PC to LAN (set IP 192.168.1.2), power off router, hold Reset + power on until LED signals U-Boot mode (AXT1800: flashes 5 times then stays solid; others: rapid blinking ~10s), release Reset, open http://192.168.1.1, upload the firmware file. AXT1800: upload factory.ubi (not .bin) — .bin will not boot. Wait 2-3 min, do not unplug.
mesh.flash_asus: Web UI > Administration > Firmware Upgrade > select factory.bin
mesh.flash_tplink: Web UI > System Tools > Firmware Upgrade > select factory.bin (Pharos interface)
mesh.flash_cudy: Download the intermediate OpenWrt firmware from cudy.com/blogs/faq/openwrt-software-download. Flash it via Cudy web UI (System > Firmware > Upload). After reboot, flash the Parahub sysupgrade.bin via LuCI (System > Backup/Flash > Flash new firmware).
mesh.flash_cudy_mirror: Parahub mirror — AP3000 Outdoor V1 (2025-11-19, for signature bypass)
mesh.flash_openwrt: System > Backup/Flash > Flash new firmware > select sysupgrade.bin
mesh.after_flash: After flashing, the router reboots and auto-configures in ~2 minutes. Connect to the Parahub_XXXX WiFi network. Check /etc/parahub/keys for credentials.

mesh.mullvad_mode_vps_desc: Guest traffic routes through VPS (Mullvad Portugal)
mesh.mullvad_mode_mullvad_desc: Guest traffic routes directly through your Mullvad account — lower latency
mesh.mullvad_setup_desc: Enter your 16-digit Mullvad account number. Optionally specify a country code (e.g. pt, de, us) or leave empty for auto-detection.
mesh.mullvad_remove_confirm: Remove local Mullvad and revert to VPS gateway?
mesh.desc_mt6000: Main gateway. 1GB RAM, 8GB storage, powerful CPU. Best choice for the central network node.
mesh.desc_axt1800: Compact gateway. Pocket-sized, easy to take anywhere. Great as a secondary gateway or for pop-up locations.
mesh.desc_mt3000: Portable gateway. Like Slate AX but with 256MB flash. Convenient for travel — plug into a hotel and share mesh.
mesh.desc_ax53u: Budget gateway. Classic home router with antennas. Good coverage at the lowest price.
mesh.desc_ap3000outdoor: Outdoor weatherproof AP with PoE. Dual-band WiFi 6 for mesh coverage in parks, courtyards and rooftops. Single PoE port doubles as WAN uplink.
mesh.desc_cpe710: Outdoor directional antenna, 23dBi. For building-to-building links up to 5+ km. 5GHz only.
mesh.desc_ar300m16: Tiny node, matchbox-sized. For short-range coverage extension in tight spots. 2.4GHz only.
mesh.speed_limit_desc: Limit free guest WiFi to the per-guest budget (512 kbps default, set in Sharing budgets)
mesh.speed_limit_enabled: Speed limit active — free guests capped at the per-guest budget
mesh.speed_limit_disabled: Speed limit off — free clients have full speed
mesh.lan_vpn_desc: Route all private network traffic through VPN
mesh.lan_vpn_disabled: Private traffic goes directly to internet
mesh.wired_mesh_desc: Use LAN port as batman-adv transport instead of regular bridge. Connect to other mesh nodes via Ethernet switch.
mesh.wired_mesh_enabled: LAN port is a batman-adv mesh interface
mesh.wired_mesh_disabled: LAN port is a regular bridge port
mesh.ygg_access_desc: Allow specific devices on your private network to be reachable from anywhere via Yggdrasil. By default, all inbound connections are blocked.
mesh.ygg_access_empty: No devices allowed — all inbound blocked
mesh.ygg_access_sync: Changes apply on next heartbeat (up to 5 minutes)
mesh.docs_architecture_desc: Each Bumblebee router creates two WiFi networks and a mesh backhaul. Batman-adv connects all routers at Layer 2. Guest traffic exits through a WireGuard VPN tunnel to a Mullvad exit node — the router owner is never the exit point.
mesh.docs_guest_flow_default: Default: Guest WiFi → WireGuard tunnel → VPS → Mullvad → Internet
mesh.docs_guest_flow_upgrade: Upgrade: Guest WiFi → Direct Mullvad WireGuard → Internet (lower latency)
mesh.docs_guest_flow_fallback: Fallback: Guest WiFi → Mesh → Nearest gateway with VPN → Internet
mesh.docs_guest_flow_desc: If the local VPN tunnel is down, the router finds another Bumblebee in the mesh that has a working tunnel and routes through it. If no gateway is available, guest internet stops (kill switch).
mesh.docs_roaming_desc: All nodes share the same SSID, password, and encryption (WPA2+WPA3). 802.11r Fast Transition enables ~50ms handoffs. 802.11k/v help clients discover and move to better access points. You walk between rooms and your device follows — no reconnection needed.
mesh.docs_ota_desc: Routers check for new firmware every night at 3 AM. If an update is available, all nodes download it first, then reboot together at XX:15 — so the mesh stays up during download. SHA256 verification prevents corrupted updates.
mesh.docs_verify_desc: After flashing, SSH into the router and check:
mesh.energy_desc: Typical power draw of each device running 24/7 with mesh, VPN and WiFi active.
mesh.energy_note: Estimates based on manufacturer specs and independent measurements. Actual consumption depends on WiFi load, number of clients, and mesh traffic.
mesh.landing_meta: Free OpenWrt firmware + EU right of access to streetlamps (GIA Reg. 2024/1309). Build a community WiFi network from ~€165 per lamppost — cover 1-2 km² for ~€2500.
mesh.landing_hero_subtitle: Ready-to-flash OpenWrt firmware + EU right of access to public streetlamps. 15 nodes cover 1-2 km². Hosts earn sats from paid guest traffic.
mesh.landing_problem_1: 850,000 Portuguese without decent internet — telcos don't invest in the «white spots» of the map
mesh.landing_problem_2: Streetlamps and electricity poles are everywhere, but local councils don't know they have an EU right to use them
mesh.landing_problem_3: Commercial solutions cost €15-30k per village — out of reach for any small council
mesh.landing_feature_1_desc: OpenWrt 25.x with zero-touch first-boot configuration. 7 supported routers, two profiles (Bumblebee gateway + Bee relay). Plug in and forget.
mesh.landing_feature_2_desc: Nodes auto-discover each other. Seamless 802.11r/k/v WiFi roaming (~50ms handoffs). Nightly OTA updates with SHA256 verification.
mesh.landing_feature_3_desc: Guest traffic exits through a WireGuard tunnel via Mullvad. You're not liable for visitor activity (EU Mere Conduit). Automatic kill switch.
mesh.landing_feature_4_desc: 512 kbps free for everyone. Guests who want full speed pay 50,000 sats for 30 days. The router removes the limit instantly — host earns passively.
mesh.landing_feature_5_desc: EU Regulation 2024/1309 (Gigabit Infrastructure Act) forces E-REDES and municipalities to grant access. In force since 12.11.2025. Request template ready.
mesh.landing_feature_6_desc: See active nodes on the Parahub map in real time. Every new router shows up automatically after first boot. No signup, no approval.
mesh.landing_how_1: Start with municipal lampposts — the council decides on its own, and a free network in general needs no operator registration. For E-REDES poles or paid traffic: file the prior notification with ANACOM — that is what makes you an operator with a legal right of access to the poles
mesh.landing_how_2: Buy 3 Cudy AP3000 Outdoor (~€270) for the pilot — your electrician wires them «before the relay» on the lamppost
mesh.landing_how_3: Plug in the PoE cable — the router auto-configures, appears in /iot and on the coverage map
mesh.eu_note: GIA — Regulation (EU) 2024/1309 — in force since 12 November 2025. Physical infrastructure owners must respond to access requests within 1 month. ANACOM arbitrates disputes with imposed pricing within 4 months. The list of valid grounds for refusal is exhaustive (6 items).
mesh.landing_free_desc: MIT licensed, no fees. Hosts earn sats, the network belongs to the community. Civic infrastructure shouldn't cost money.

peering.title: Mesh Peering Agreement
peering.meta_desc: The peering agreement governing free transit on the Parahub mesh — adopted from the Pico Peering Agreement v1.0.
peering.draft_text: This agreement is a working draft pending legal review and is not yet in force. The wording may change.
peering.intro: This agreement governs the free transit that Parahub mesh nodes donate to one another and to guests. It is separate from the firmware's software licence (MIT) and from the platform Terms of Service.
peering.adopted: Sections 1–4 and the definitions below are the {ppa}, maintained by volunteers at picopeer.net and reproduced verbatim. Section 5 contains Parahub's local amendments, as the PPA template intends.
preamble: There are now many community networks, but they are seperated geographically and socially and do not form a coherent network. This document is an attempt to connect those network islands by providing the minimum baseline template for a peering agreement between owners of individual network nodes - the Pico Peering Agreement.

The PPA is a way of formalizing the interaction between two peers. Owners of network nodes assert their right of ownership by declaring their willingness to donate the free exchange of data across their networks.
The PPA is maintained at picopeer.net by a group of volunteers from around the world. It is intended to be used as a template for other small-scale peering documents and licenses.
s1: The owner agrees to provide free transit accross their free network.
The owner agrees not to modify or interfere with data as it passes through their free network.
s2: The owner agrees to publish the information necessary for peering to take place
This information shall be published under a free licence
The owner agrees to be contactable and will provide at least an email adress
s3: There is no guaranteed level of service
The service is provided "as is", with no warranty or liability of whatsoever kind
The service can be scaled back or withdrawn at any time with no notice
s4: The owner is entitled to formulate an 'acceptable use policy'
This may or may not contain information about additional services provided (apart from basic access)
The owner is free to formulate this policy as long as it does not contradict points 1 to 3 of this agreement (see point 5)
peering.amend_intro: For Parahub mesh nodes, this section is completed as follows. It does not alter points 1–4: every service or limit below is introduced under point 4 (Terms of Use / Additional Services) and, where it restricts the Service, under point 3 (the owner's right to scale back or withdraw it).
amend: 5.1 Additional Services. Beyond Free Transit, Parahub Bumblebee nodes may provide guests with DHCP, encrypted DNS (DoH — resolved locally, with Cloudflare / Google as an upstream fallback only), guest isolation, best-effort traffic management, and a VPN-tunnelled internet exit. Each is an "Additional Service" in the sense of point 4 and the definitions — offered over and above, and without displacing, the Free Transit of point 1.

5.2 Traffic management (net neutrality). Any bandwidth shaping is best-effort, content-neutral, and applied solely for network stability and fair resource sharing, consistent with Regulation (EU) 2015/2120 on open-internet access. It is a management measure under point 3, not interference with the content of data under point 1.

5.3 Paid capacity. The base tier of guest access is provided free of charge and is Free Transit within the meaning of point 1. Throughput above that free tier may be offered as an optional, separately purchased Additional Service (for example, via Lightning); charging for this optional capacity is not a charge for Free Transit.
5.4 Acceptable use. Guests must not use the network for unlawful activity, network attacks, or abuse. Per point 3, access may be scaled back or withdrawn at any time without notice.

5.5 Egress / mere-conduit. Guest traffic egresses to the open internet from the IP address of a VPN gateway — by default a Parahub gateway whose own exit is a commercial VPN provider located in Portugal, or a VPN account the node owner has configured directly on the node — and never from a node owner's own public IP address. The encrypted tunnel traverses the owner's access line, but the owner does not originate that traffic, choose its recipient, or modify it, and so acts solely as an intermediary conduit («simples transporte») under Article 14 of Decreto-Lei 7/2004 (transposing Directive 2000/31/EC) and Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act). If a node's own tunnel is unavailable, its guest traffic may cross the mesh and egress through another node's tunnel; if neither a tunnel nor a mesh gateway can be reached, guest traffic is isolated (no internet).

5.6 The Association. Parahub — Associação (NIPC 519 190 904) publishes and maintains these amendments and operates the shared VPN egress. In respect of that egress it likewise acts as a mere conduit under the instruments cited in 5.5, and will respond to lawful requests and abuse notices addressed to the egress operator in accordance with Articles 12–13 of Decreto-Lei 7/2004. To the maximum extent permitted by applicable mandatory law, the Association is not a party to, and assumes no liability for, the transit traffic of guests or nodes.

5.7 Data protection. Nodes send a periodic heartbeat carrying technical and network data: hardware and MAC identifiers, node keys, firmware version, connection status and throughput counters, and — from the node that terminates the guest network — the current guest DHCP leases (WiFi address (MAC), local IP, and the hostname the device announces itself under). Guest leases are what allows a full-speed pass to be applied to the right device; they are held as current state only, each heartbeat replacing the previous snapshot, and are not accumulated into a history. Guest traffic itself is neither inspected nor logged. A node's location may be shown on the public coverage map only with the owner's consent, and the owner is named there only on explicit opt-in. The Association, as operator of the egress, processes the minimum connection metadata needed to run the service. Processing follows Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR); the controller roles, retention, and logging position are set out in the Parahub Privacy Policy, which forms part of these terms.

5.8 Non-profit operation. The mesh is run by a non-profit association on a community basis, to donate and sustain Free Transit. The Additional Services exist to secure and maintain the network. The base tier of guest access is free of charge, and full-speed access can also be earned without paying for it; where optional capacity above the free tier is paid for (5.3), the payment is received by the Association and goes to the shared infrastructure. The Association takes no share of transit and no percentage of anything that passes over the mesh.

5.9 Governing law and scope. This Agreement is governed by the law of Portugal, and the competent Portuguese courts have jurisdiction — without prejudice to any mandatory protection or forum a consumer may have under their local law. Point 5.5 describes the network's architecture and the legal position of nodes operated in Portugal; it is not a warranty of any particular liability regime for nodes operated elsewhere, whose owners remain subject to their local law.

5.10 Limitation and severability. The exclusions of warranty and liability in point 3 apply only to the extent permitted by applicable mandatory law — including consumer-protection rules, the regime on standard contract terms (Decreto-Lei 446/85), and Article 809 of the Civil Code. If any provision of this section is held invalid, the remainder stays in force.

5.11 Acceptance and versioning. This document is versioned; material changes are published before they take effect. Flashing Parahub mesh firmware and operating a node on the mesh constitutes the owner's acceptance of the version in force. While this document is marked "not yet effective", no acceptance is sought and nothing in it binds a node owner.
defs: Owner — The owner of the node has the right to operate their network equipment and to donate any part of its functionality to the FreeNetwork
Transit — Transit is the exchange of data into, out of or across a network
Free Transit — Free transit means that the owner will neither charge for the transit of data nor modify the data
Free Network — The Free Network is the sum of interconnected hardware and software resources, whose FreeTransit has been donated by the owners of those resources
The Service — The Service is made up of Free transit and Additional Services
Additional Services — In terms of the PPA, an additional service is anything over and above Free Transit. For example, provision of a DHCP server, a web server or a mail server
peering.practice: The PPA shall be implemented in data readable form following agreed standards in community network node data bases to facilitate automatic interconnection of nodes.
peering.attribution: Sections 1–4 and the definitions are the Pico Peering Agreement v1.0, released under CC0 (public domain) and reproduced from {source} verbatim (original spelling preserved). Section 5 (Local Amendments) is © Parahub — Associação (NIPC 519 190 904).

mesh.free_privacy_text: To give your device the speed you paid for or earned, the node reports its WiFi address (MAC), local IP and the name the device announces to the network. That is kept as a current snapshot only — the next report replaces it, nothing is accumulated into a history. Your traffic itself is not inspected or logged, and it leaves through a VPN tunnel.
